title: Razborov decoding inverts encoding on bad restrictions
statement: Let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables whose width is at most $w$, and suppose that no term of $f$ contains two distinct literals on the same variable (within each term, any two literals sharing a variable coincide). Let $\rho$ be a restriction that is bad for $f$ at depth $d$, meaning the restriction of the Boolean function computed by $f$ along $\rho$ has decision-tree depth strictly greater than $d$. Writing $(\gamma, \mathrm{aux})$ for the pair produced by the Razborov encoding of $f$, $w$, $d$, $\rho$, the Razborov decoding of $(\gamma, \mathrm{aux})$ with parameters $f$ and $w$ returns the original restriction $\rho$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a DNF formula on n variables
width of f is at most w (f.width ≤ w)
within each term of f, literals on the same variable are equal (non-degeneracy)
ρ is a bad restriction for f's Boolean function at depth d
replaced:
For a width-$w$ DNF $f$ with distinct variables per term and a bad restriction $\rho$ for
$f.\mathrm{eval}$ at depth $d$, decoding the Razborov encoding of $\rho$ returns $\rho$:
$\mathrm{razborovDecode}\ f\ w\ (\mathrm{razborovEncode}\ f\ w\ d\ \rho) = \rho$.
